outcome: composite outcome of cerebral palsy, epilepsy, mental retardation, and death
cohort: 505,075 live term born infants without congenital malformations or chromosomal abnormalities in Sweden from 2009 to 2015.
finding: Mild neonatal hypoxic ischaemic encephalopathy was associated with a four-fold increased risk of a composite outcome of cerebral palsy, epilepsy, mental retardation, and death up to 6 years of age.
